p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked PDH readout that a PDK inhibitor moves (PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation, PDH activity, glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling) in WWOX-deficient against matched control human neural cells, read as a genotype-by-inhibitor interaction; and, only after that, the glucose, lactate, ketone and alanine time course in Wwox-null pups before any seizure or behavioural endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for any PDK inhibitor in a WWOX system. In non-WWOX epilepsy models: no anticonvulsant effect and a slight pro-convulsant signal in a mouse study (abstract); a histological neuroprotection result for the DCA plus pyruvate combination in rats after seizure. In children with congenital lactic acidosis: lactate lowering without clinical benefit over six months in a randomized trial.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: The Wwox-null mouse is hypoglycaemic from the first postnatal week and dies within weeks, so a pup experiment runs in the same window as the lethal phenotype and is survivor-conditioned; neuron-specific deletion survival is not established here. The seizure and glucose precedents are adult animals or adult humans except the paediatric mitochondrial-disease trials.

cellular_context.target_expression: PDK isoforms are expressed in brain; the WWOX-dependent level is UNKNOWN. PDK1 transcript is lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null) in two human neural transcript systems and higher in mouse and human non-neural cells.
cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: No WWOX-deficient human neural system has a PDH activity or phosphorylation measurement.
cellular_context.limits: Transcript results are not PDH activity. A raised glycolytic signature does not prove a PDH block. PDH restraint is documented after chemoconvulsant status epilepticus in non-WWOX models, which a WWOX-DEE brain may share independent of genotype.

input.axis: I / IT5 P9: useful partial benefit, PDK inhibition (dichloroacetate): premise, seizure endpoint, glycaemia

mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: A downstream metabolic bypass: partial benefit at best, only if a PDH restraint exists; the card tests the premise and the safety side, it does not propose a treatment. Track B: no allele-specific rationale.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

p4_card.identity: Dichloroacetate (DCA), the prototype pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK) inhibitor: catalogue records CAT:CHEMBL306823 (sodium dichloroacetate, ChEMBL mechanism rows INHIBITOR at PDK1 to PDK4, clinical candidate, access: experimental), CAT:DGIDB:901979e6ba30 (sodium dichloroacetate, DGIdb, status unverified) and CAT:CHEMBL13960 and CAT:DGIDB:b7c34486f9a7 (the acid, no ChEMBL target rows). Identity by identifier: the card asserts CHEMBL306823 only. DCA is an investigational drug with an orphan designation for congenital lactic acidosis; it has no marketed label in openFDA (searches by generic name and active ingredient returned no match on 2026-10-29). Whether any product is sold to consumers as a dietary ingredient was not established here and is handed to the supplement-access worker; access is not efficacy or safety. Related ingredients that act on the same enzyme step through cofactors or substrates (thiamine, alpha-lipoic acid, pyruvate) are not asserted by this card.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Not an indication and not a treatment proposal. The card asks what has to be true for a PDK inhibitor to be a partial-benefit lever in a Wwox-deficient brain (a measured PDH restraint that the inhibitor releases), whether the one seizure endpoint tested in a PDH-restrained epilepsy model was favourable (it was not), and which way the glucose endpoint moves in a setting with documented hypoglycaemia. Nothing measured in a mitochondrial-disease population, an adult epilepsy mouse, a diabetic adult or a large animal is transferred to WWOX-DEE.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: PARZIALMENTE_TROVATO: DCA is on the map (record N-08, parked after the peripheral-nerve narrowing; card E03 holds target-engagement rows and no disease-side PDH datum) and the DCA-with-pyruvate rat seizure paper is read. Not previously in the repository, by a search of the registries' PMID fields and the research notes on 2026-10-29: the primary mouse seizure-endpoint test of DCA (PMID 29913407), the two randomized paediatric and MELAS trials as efficacy evidence (16651305, 16476929 is cited in a trial note only), the glucose-direction literature (625308, 3521930, 35730570, 10546922, 8052155), and the human fibroblast PDK transcript sentence (PMID 35328751). Not 'never done': only PubMed, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov, openFDA and the catalogue were searched.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: Card E03 (PDK inhibition, unresolved; translation fields all UNKNOWN); map record N-08 (parked: nerve conduction signal, no WWOX measurement); needs NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS (direction uncertain; 'do not treat dichloroacetate as evidence-backed'), NEED-LACTATE-LDH, NEED-SEIZURE-CONTROL-SYMPTOMATIC, NEED-SYSTEMIC-GLYCAEMIA-GROWTH (endpoint and confounder; no compounds by design); card E04 and EB-KD-01 for the ketogenic diet (three depths already, not repeated); the systems comparison of 2026-10-29 (PDK1 lower in both human neural transcript systems, glycolysis and LDHA higher in both).
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE, Track A (variant-independent, downstream, allele-blind). Metabolic bypass: partial benefit at best, and only if the bottleneck exists. Safety side: glycaemia and peripheral nerve.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN as benefit. The card sharpens a decision: it separates 'a raised glycolytic signature' (LDHA and a hand-picked HIF-type gene set higher in two human neural transcript systems, a broader 19-gene panel inside the null in the progenitor line) from 'PDH is restrained' (no WWOX activity or phosphorylation datum, PDK1 lower in sign only and inside its single-gene null, PDH activity unchanged in one human line, brain lactate low in one patient) and from 'releasing PDH helps' (no seizure benefit in the only PDH-restrained model tested; no clinical benefit in a randomized paediatric trial despite lactate lowering). If a WWOX-deficient neural system shows an inhibitor-responsive PDH restraint, the lever moves from parked to testable with a defined safety frame; if not, the PDK strand of the module is closed at the premise.
p4_card.mechanism: DCA inhibits PDK isoforms (ChEMBL curated mechanism, enzyme level, potency not reproduced here), lowering inhibitory phosphorylation of PDH and so raising glucose oxidation at the expense of lactate; it also inhibits its own metabolising enzyme (glutathione transferase zeta 1), which makes exposure rise on repeated administration and vary with haplotype and age. The WWOX-side chain proposes WWOX loss, HIF1alpha, PDK1, PDH inhibition and a glycolytic shift. Evidence for the chain, by link: HIF1alpha up and glycolytic shift in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (mouse, non-neural); PDK1 up in the same cells; PDK transcript up in a human knockout fibroblast line; PDK1 lower in sign only (inside the single-gene null) in two human neural transcript systems; PDH activity not different in the human fibroblast line; no PDH phosphorylation, flux or lactate measurement in any WWOX-deficient human neural system. Competing explanations for a raised-lactate, normal-PDH-activity state: supply-side glycolytic overflow (hexokinase and LDH activity higher in the same cells), maturity of the tissue (organoid), and a secondary PDH restraint that follows chemoconvulsant status epilepticus, which is documented in wild-type animals in two epilepsy models (rat after pilocarpine seizure: PDK2 up, PDH down, Ser293 phosphorylation up; mouse chronic stage: PDH activity down by about two thirds). The last point matters for the symptom claim: a WWOX-DEE brain with seizures may carry a PDH restraint that arises after seizure and status-epilepticus injury (not separable from neuron loss or drug exposure in either model), which the seizure-endpoint test (DR-I01-002 to -004) addresses directly and found no anticonvulsant effect.

ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-29: 27 records for dichloroacetate; relevant: NCT02616484 (phase 3, pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency, active), NCT06931262 (expanded access for that condition), NCT00068913 (MELAS), NCT03356457 (type 1 diabetes and hypoglycaemia); none in a WWOX or epilepsy population
openFDA drug label API: no match for dichloroacetate by generic name or active ingredient, 2026-10-29

for: The WWOX-side chain is real at its two ends: HK activity, LDH activity and lactate are higher in a human knockout fibroblast line, and LDHA and a hand-picked HIF-type gene set are higher in two human neural transcript systems (a broader 19-gene panel is inside the null in the progenitor line), and PDK1 is reported up in Wwox-null mouse cells; so a PDK-PDH restraint is not excluded.

In two independent epilepsy models the PDK-PDH restraint is documented (rat after seizure; mouse chronic stage), and a combination of DCA and pyruvate protected hippocampal neurons after seizure in rats (histology, not seizure control); a review reports protection against hypoglycaemia-induced neuronal injury in rats (second-hand).

Cerebrospinal fluid lactate fell in the long-term paediatric follow-up (drug exposure in the CNS not measured: CNS exposure stays UNKNOWN) and DCA has a documented paediatric safety record in congenital lactic acidosis (a randomized trial, a follow-up of 110 patient-years, an expanded access route for pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency).

The response to the inhibitor is genotype dependent in cells (patient cells with a PDH defect shifted, control cells did not), which makes a genotype-by-inhibitor experiment in WWOX-deficient cells informative in both directions.
against: No WWOX-deficient neural system has a PDH activity, PDH phosphorylation, flux or lactate measurement; PDK1 transcript is not higher in either human neural system held (lower in sign only, inside the single-gene null: organoid p about 0.30, one shRNA progenitor library at n = 1 per arm p about 0.49; neurons +0.44) and the human fibroblast PDH activity is unchanged; brain lactate is reported extremely low in the one patient with MRS.

The PDK transcript sign is cell-type dependent (up in mouse and human non-neural cells, lower in sign only in the neural transcript systems); each comparison has a different confound, and the contrast cannot be turned into a statement about WWOX.

The only primary seizure-endpoint test found of DCA in a PDH-restrained epilepsy model (mouse, chronic pilocarpine; PDH activity down by about two thirds) showed no anticonvulsant effect and a slight pro-convulsant signal in one test (abstract level). The rat protection result is a histology endpoint and uses the combination with pyruvate (the Discussion of that paper cites earlier work for the inactivity of the single agents).

A randomized double-blind paediatric trial (43 children, heterogeneous mitochondrial disease) lowered post-meal lactate and moved none of the clinical outcomes measured (global assessment, linear growth, intercurrent illness) over six months; the MELAS trial was terminated early for peripheral nerve toxicity; the long-term cohort shows conduction slowing and a below-first-percentile growth trajectory, not separable from the disease.

The glucose endpoint: the Wwox-null mouse is hypoglycaemic (lethally so in one laboratory's description) with higher glucose uptake in knockout cells, and DCA lowers fasting glucose in diabetic adults while lowering the gluconeogenic precursors lactate and alanine; three of four datasets point to glucose lowering (diabetic adults; endotoxaemic minipigs, deeper hypoglycaemia through lower hepatic glucose output; cirrhotic and healthy adults, a modest fall in glucose production and plasma glucose in both groups) and only the septic mouse shows reversal, alongside reversal of anorexia and with plasma lactate lower, not higher, in the septic mice. The sign for a Wwox-deficient pup is unmeasured. Hypoglycaemia is also confounded in the null with feeding and seizures.

Exposure is variable by design: DCA inactivates its own clearing enzyme, clearance depends on haplotype and age, and a population model finds the inactivation rate lower in children than adults by a large factor; a monitoring requirement (nerve conduction) is part of the long-term paediatric protocol.

A thiamine-linked rat observation (oxalate and neuropathy) and one methaemoglobinaemia case report in a glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-deficient neonate (case report, abstract) are further safety notes; neither is WWOX-specific.

IT7 P3/P1 (exploratory, independently verified): the six-gene module under the glycolytic end of the chain was inconclusive in an independent WWOX-loss contrast (P47T hippocampus, p 0.060, inside its null; PDK1 lower by -0.08, not raised), and a signed network and a WWOX-enriched network showed no added value for ranking compounds on it while a signature route was not detected, not excluded (rho 0.143 against a 0.15 threshold; interval 0.039 to 0.243); dichloroacetate was outside that comparison by design. A computational result, not engagement or efficacy data.

p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Catalogue: experimental for the sodium salt (ChEMBL), status unverified in DGIdb; no marketed label in openFDA; a pivotal phase 3 for pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency is active and an expanded access protocol exists for that diagnosis only (ClinicalTrials.gov, 2026-10-29). Whether a product is sold as a supplement is not established here and is handed over; if one is found, product-level facts do not make the substance evidence-backed or safe. No contact was made.
p4_card.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN, separately from access. No benefit endpoint is pursued by this card. In the paediatric randomized trial the time frame of the clinical outcomes was six months and none moved; post-meal lactate moved within that window.
p4_card.pharmacology: Mechanism-based irreversible-type self-inhibition of metabolism (glutathione transferase zeta 1 inactivation): repeated administration shifts every subject towards slow metabolism, with a two-fold faster inactivation in subjects lacking a wild-type haplotype and a 25 to 30 fold lower inactivation rate in children than adults in one population model (abstract level); drug kinetics in 17 children plateaued rather than accumulating. Metabolites include oxalate (a 22% rise in urinary oxalate in the long-term cohort) and tyrosine-pathway intermediates (maleylacetone, delta-aminolevulinate rise in the randomized trial). Peripheral neuropathy is the dose-limiting toxicity in adults with MELAS; hepatotoxicity and neoplasia are rodent findings at high chronic doses (1998 review abstract). Oral route in the trials; Cerebrospinal fluid lactate fell in the long-term cohort; CNS drug exposure was not measured. No dose, route or schedule is stated or implied here. Not a label (no label exists).
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Paediatric trial and long-term experience exist only in congenital lactic acidosis; no data in epilepsy, DEE or WWOX. Interactions with antiseizure medicines and with a ketogenic diet are not characterised here (the long-term cohort notes children with PDH deficiency not on ketogenic diets maintained normal lactate on DCA). The glucose interaction with fasting, a ketogenic diet and feeding difficulty is the question this card raises, not an answer.

scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: WWOX rows: three transcript results (two computational re-analyses, n = 1 and 4 versus 2; one qPCR sentence), one enzyme null, one mouse glucose set from two laboratories. Everything else is another disease, species or compound. Shared sources are not independent confirmations.

question_history: Mandate IT5, step P9 (scientist-d, 2026-10-29): partial benefit as a thread distinct from vigabatrin (cards H02, EB-VGB-01). Candidates weighed by data: the ketogenic diet (worked at three depths; open items are denominator and metabolic measurements), lithium (G01) and apinocaltamide (H01) already had closed loops, stiripentol (E02) is fully worked in P2a, the glucose and growth need has no compound by design. Chosen: the PDK strand, because the new systems comparison removed its middle link (PDK1 not up) while card E03 still carried an open translation block, and because a literature search from the compound found primary seizure, efficacy and glucose data not yet in the repository.

Need-to-compound search (NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS, NEED-LACTATE-LDH, NEED-REDOX-OXIDATIVE-STRESS, NEED-NEUROINFLAMMATION-GLIA) and compound-to-WWOX-profile search (dichloroacetate, thiamine, alpha-lipoic acid, pyruvate, beta-hydroxybutyrate, decanoic acid, carnitine) are in the cycle README.

IT7 P6 (2026-10-29): the six-gene module did not transfer decisively to an independent WWOX-loss contrast and the network routes showed no added value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded (loop_demonstration_it7_p6_20261029/README.md; P3 numbers independently verified). Status, F/C/P position and the premise are unchanged.
p4_card.predictions: Registered before any such experiment, two directions each. (1) In WWOX-deficient human neural cells against isogenic or transduction-matched controls at matched maturity, with PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation and PDH activity measured first: if a PDH restraint exists, a PDK inhibitor raises PDH activity and glucose-derived acetyl-CoA labelling more in the deficient cells than in controls (genotype-by-inhibitor interaction), and basal phosphorylation is higher in the deficient cells; if there is no restraint, basal phosphorylation and activity do not differ and the inhibitor shifts both genotypes alike or neither, and the PDK strand is closed at the premise. (2) In a Wwox-deficient pup model that survives the window, with wild-type littermates, a PDK inhibitor against vehicle at confirmed brain exposure: three outcome categories for glucose against vehicle, read in wild-type and deficient pups separately: (i) a fall in the deficient pups beyond the wild-type fall, as in the minipig, with lactate and, if measured, alanine falling, which would end the in vivo thread on safety grounds; (ii) a modest fall of similar size in both genotypes, as in adults, which is a liability whose weight depends on baseline glucose and is read against the hypoglycaemic baseline; (iii) no fall or a rise, as in the septic mouse, which is read only together with food intake; either way glucose is the first readout, before any seizure or behavioural endpoint. A negative with unconfirmed brain exposure is uninformative.
p4_card.next_measurement: IT7 P6 2026-10-29: decisive measurement unchanged; read PDK1, LDHA, LDHB, HK2, SLC2A1 and BNIP3 transcripts beside it in the same cells, so the replicated WWOX-deficient human neural contrast that the P3 comparison named as missing is also a second transfer test; no computational ranking selects the compound arm. Cells: PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation (and total PDH), PDH activity, and a glucose-tracer experiment into acetyl-CoA, citrate and lactate in WWOX-deficient human neural cells against matched controls, then with a PDK inhibitor against vehicle, reading the genotype-by-inhibitor interaction; IT8 P3 2026-10-29: dichloroacetate inhibits the recombinant human kinase isoforms only at high concentrations in curated database rows (from about 0.1 millimolar for the most sensitive isoform to above 5 millimolar for the least, unknown-origin enzymes, with the same isoform differing about 7 to 18 fold between laboratories), so a null with it at cell-attainable concentrations cannot separate 'the kinase does not matter' from 'the kinase was not inhibited'; the premise experiment therefore uses an inhibitor of nanomolar potency (curated target rows; every retrieved qualifying molecule is listed by id in pharmacological_qualification_it8_p3_20261029/measures_detail.tsv, not ranked, and the kinase pulls are truncated; availability and neuronal engagement are not shown) as the probe and dichloroacetate as the clinically known comparator, with the free exposure of each measured. Animal, only if the cell result shows restraint: blood glucose, lactate, ketones and alanine time course in P10 to P14 Wwox-null pups against wild-type littermates, inhibitor against vehicle, with brain exposure confirmed and feeding recorded, before any seizure endpoint. Human, no contact made: a structured count of WWOX-DEE children who have had metabolic screens, brain MRS or a ketogenic diet, with glucose events and lactate values (denominator), from the natural history; a registry query of the investigational-drug programme for pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency is not a WWOX measure.
p4_card.value_added: Turns the PDK strand from 'parked, safety-narrowed' into a premise test with a stated closing condition; adds the primary seizure-endpoint negative and the randomized paediatric efficacy null to the repository; flags the glucose endpoint as a sign-unresolved liability in a model whose lethal phenotype is hypoglycaemia (the earlier safety framing was nerve-only); records that PDK transcript direction differs between non-neural cells (up) and neural transcript systems (not higher; lower in sign only) and that the human fibroblast paper's own sentence on 'PDK activity' is a wording flag, and corrects the glucose set (the cirrhosis study shows a modest fall in both groups); and records the supplement-class ingredients near the same enzyme step for access work.
p4_card.clinical_census: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-29, query by intervention 'dichloroacetate': 27 records (congenital lactic acidosis phase 2 and 3, pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency phase 3 active, an expanded access protocol, MELAS, cancers, type 1 diabetes and hypoglycaemia physiology, healthy-volunteer pharmacokinetics); none in a WWOX, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy or epilepsy population. Earlier census 2026-10-20 found no registered WOREE interventional study. A missing hit does not prove that no study exists.

not_known: Whether PDH is phosphorylated (restrained) in any WWOX-deficient neural system, human or mouse, and whether a PDK inhibitor releases it more than in control cells.
Whether the PDK transcript sign difference between non-neural lines (up) and neural transcript systems (down) is biology or confound.

The direction of the blood glucose response to a PDK inhibitor in a hypoglycaemic Wwox-deficient pup (pig-like deepening or mouse-sepsis-like reversal), and whether the null's hypoglycaemia is hepatic, feeding-related or seizure-related.
Whether the seizure-endpoint negative in the adult mouse holds in a developmental model or at confirmed brain exposure (the study is abstract-level and closed).
Brain lactate and PDH state in WWOX-DEE patients (one MRS report with a confounding variant); any metabolic screen denominator.
Whether any consumer product contains dichloroacetate or the related cofactor ingredients, and with what content; access is not evidence.
evidence_against: Transcripts, not activity: the chain is supported at its glycolytic end and without support in its middle (PDK1 not higher, lower in sign only and inside its null, in two human neural systems; PDH activity unchanged in the one human line).
Seizure-secondary PDH restraint is documented in two non-WWOX epilepsy models, so any restraint found in a seizing WWOX brain would not by itself be WWOX-dependent.

The one primary seizure test of the lever found in a PDH-restrained model was negative (abstract level); the one randomized paediatric trial moved lactate and no clinical outcome; the one randomized MELAS trial ended early for nerve toxicity.

Hypoglycaemia is the Wwox-null phenotype and the lever lowers glucose in adults with raised glucose and lowers gluconeogenic precursors; the weight of the glucose datasets points to lowering (pig, adults), with one mouse reversal that coincides with feeding recovery; the sign in a hypoglycaemic young animal is unmeasured.
Rivals for the raised-lactate observations: supply-side glycolytic overflow, tissue maturity (organoid), line differences, and feeding or seizure state in animals.

bridge_gaps_exposed: No drug row is in a context matching a WWOX row, so the bridge forms no sign comparison (UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology).
The bridge cannot express a group-difference null that sits beside a within-group change (the cirrhosis study: both groups fell, the groups did not differ); the limit lives in the notes.
The bridge has no field for a lever whose benefit depends on a precondition (PDH restraint); the precondition lives in the card text and the predictions.

p4_roadmap_fields.indication_and_transfer: Not an indication and not a treatment proposal. The card asks what has to be true for a PDK inhibitor to be a partial-benefit lever in a Wwox-deficient brain (a measured PDH restraint that the inhibitor releases), whether the one seizure endpoint tested in a PDH-restrained epilepsy model was favourable (it was not), and which way the glucose endpoint moves in a setting with documented hypoglycaemia. Nothing measured in a mitochondrial-disease population, an adult epilepsy mouse, a diabetic adult or a large animal is transferred to WWOX-DEE.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No ranking, probability or blended index is carried.
directional_summary compares signs only where target, endpoint and every context dimension match; UNRESOLVED is a statement about the record, not about the biology.
